newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian judge to give verdict on Gandhi "marriage".
newsitem.headline: Indian judge to give verdict on Gandhi "marriage".

text.p: An Indian judge said he would give his verdict on Tuesday in a case in which a man claims to have married the daughter of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and she has denied it.
Civil Judge Vipin Gupta on Monday threw out a plea by V. Ramakrishnan Goud in which Goud sought a medical examination of Priyanka Gandhi, 25, which he said would prove they had married in 1991.
Earlier on Monday, a lawyer representing Gandhi, often regarded as her father's political heir, submitted a written petition in which she denied the marriage.
Goud himself was brought to Gupta's court under judicial custody in a separate case. He is accused of using offensive language against low-caste Hindus in his southern state of Andhra Pradesh.
Gandhi plans to marry Delhi businessman Robert Wadhera on February 5 but was forced to go to the court after Goud claimed she could not do so because she was still his wife.
Gandhi's lawyers have described Goud's claim as "false and frivolous".

After Rajiv Gandhi was killed by a woman suicide bomber in May 1991, senior leaders of his Congress party turned to his Italian-born widow Sonia Gandhi to become the party's president. But the media-shy and self-effacing Sonia Gandhi has kept largely aloof from public life.

Some newspapers have said that Priyanka Gandhi, whom they liken to her grandmother and former prime minister Indira Gandhi, was the next choice for the Congress to keep the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty in the country's political limelight.
Priyanka Gandhi has a 27-year old brother. But Congress sources say he is not interested in politics.
